title: Vertical divisors of a smooth morphism with geometrically integral fibres
statement:
Let $S$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $p:X\to S$ be a separated smooth morphism of finite presentation from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with every geometric fibre nonempty and integral. These properties of a space morphism are tested on etale scheme charts; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $V\subseteq S$ be dense and open [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $X$ is regular and locally Noetherian, and $X_V$ is dense in $X$. Over any affine open $B\subseteq S$, the space $X_B$ is Noetherian and separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

Write $\operatorname{Div}_{S\setminus V}(S)$ for the group of locally finite integral sums of integral codimension-one closed subschemes supported in $S\setminus V$, and define $\operatorname{Div}_{X\setminus X_V}(X)$ in the same way using codimension on etale charts. Flat Cartier pullback identifies these groups:
$$p^*: \operatorname{Div}_{S\setminus V}(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Div}_{X\setminus X_V}(X).$$
More precisely, every prime divisor of $X$ disjoint from $X_V$ is $p^{-1}(Z)$ for a unique prime divisor $Z$ of $S$ disjoint from $V$, with reduced structure; $p^{-1}(Z)$ is integral and has multiplicity one in $p^*Z$. Cartier divisors here mean sections of the sheaf of nonzero rational functions modulo regular units, which agree with the indicated locally finite Weil divisors on a regular space. The assertions are local on $S$. For every etale map $a:S'\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], $S'$ is regular locally Noetherian, $V'=a^{-1}V$ is dense, and the base-changed $p':X\times_SS'\to S'$ again satisfies the hypotheses. The divisor identifications commute with these etale base changes.

proof.text: Work over an affine open $B\subset S$. By the chartwise calculus, $p$ is flat, and its base changes and its composites with etale scheme charts are smooth. For an affine chart $U\to X_B$, the map to $B$ corresponds to a smooth ring map by the affine smoothness comparison. The coordinate ring of $B$ is regular (or restrict further to the regular affine neighborhoods in the definition); smooth ascent makes $U$ regular. Thus every chart of $X$ is regular and locally Noetherian. Finite presentation makes $X_B$ quasi-compact, and separatedness over $B$ makes it quasi-separated. Hence $X_B$ is Noetherian in the sense used in the item. The affine scheme $B$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; composition of separated space morphisms makes $X_B$ separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. These observations verify all hypotheses of the divisor dictionary on both $B$ and $X_B$.

proof.text: The geometric-fibre hypothesis implies surjectivity of $|p|$: a point of a geometric fibre gives a point above its base point. Ordinary fibres are nonempty and irreducible as well: extension from a residue field to its algebraic closure is surjective on points, and the continuous image of the irreducible geometric fibre is irreducible. To verify the surjectivity on charts, tensor with the field extension, use faithful flatness and surjectivity on spectra, and then the point calculus for the atlas. Ordinary fibres are reduced because they are smooth over fields, by smooth reduced ascent. The flat locally finitely presented space map $p$ is universally open. If $O\subset X$ is a nonempty open, $p(O)$ is nonempty open, so it meets $V$ and consequently $O$ meets $X_V$. This proves the asserted density. The same argument applies to every open restriction on $S$.

proof.text: Let $Z\subset B$ be any integral closed subscheme and put $Y=X_B\times_B Z$. It is reduced by smooth reduced ascent and is quasi-separated. Its map $q:Y\to Z$ is surjective and open, with nonempty irreducible fibres by Step 2. For nonempty opens $O_1,O_2\subset Y$, their images are nonempty opens in the irreducible space $Z$, so choose $z\in q(O_1)\cap q(O_2)$. The two fibre intersections are nonempty opens in the irreducible fibre $Y_z$ and therefore intersect. Thus $Y$ is irreducible. The field-monomorphism lemma gives a quasi-compact monomorphism from a field representing every point of $Y$: this is the pointwise decency condition (Tag 03JV, condition (4)). Thus $Y$ is decent. Together with reducedness and irreducibility this says $Y$ is integral. Soberness gives its unique generic point $y$. Moreover $q(y)=\eta_Z$: if $T\subset Z$ is nonempty open, $q^{-1}T$ is nonempty open and contains $y$. This argument does not require $Z$ regular or the charts of $Y$ irreducible. Closed inverse-image supports have their usual meaning by the reduced-closed-support theorem.

proof.text:
Let $W$ be a prime divisor of $X_B$ disjoint from $X_V$, with generic point $\xi$, and put $s=p(\xi)$. Choose an affine etale chart through $\xi$ and then an affine open in it. Its point $u$ above $\xi$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}=1$ by the chart definition of codimension. On a regular affine base neighborhood the flat height formula applies to the Noetherian coordinate rings and gives
$$1=\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}+\dim\mathcal O_{U_s,u}.$$
The point $s$ is outside $V$. Every generic point of the locally Noetherian base lies in its dense open $V$; hence $\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}>0$. Therefore it equals one and the fibre local dimension is zero. Set $Z=\overline{\{s\}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ in $B$. It is a prime divisor disjoint from $V$ (the complement is closed). The fibre point represented by $\xi$ is generic in $X_s$: otherwise a strict generization lifts to a strict generization of $u$ on an etale fibre chart, contradicting its zero-dimensional local ring. Here use the sober and etale-specialization statements for the separated fibre. Since $X_s$ is irreducible, this generic point is unique.

proof.text: For $Z$ from Step 4, Step 3 makes $Y=p^{-1}(Z)$ integral. Its generic point lies over $s=\eta_Z$ and is therefore the generic point of $X_s$, namely $\xi$. Thus $|Y|=\overline{\{\xi\}}=|W|$. Both are reduced closed subspaces of $X_B$, so the uniqueness clause for reduced closed supports gives $Y=W$ as closed subspaces. Conversely, for any prime divisor $Z\subset B$ outside $V$, Step 3 gives an integral $Y=p^{-1}(Z)$ whose generic point lies over $\eta_Z$. On an etale fibre chart at that generic point, there are no strict generizations: a strict generization in the chart would give one in the fibre, or two comparable points with the same image, both excluded by the etale-specialization theorem. Thus the fibre local dimension is zero. The flat height formula now gives $\delta_{X_B}(\eta_Y)=1+0=1$, so $Y$ is a prime divisor. Surjectivity of $p$ gives uniqueness of $Z$, since the image of $p^{-1}|Z|$ is exactly $|Z|$.

proof.text: Let $Z\subset B$ be a prime divisor disjoint from $V$, with generic point $s$. The local rings of the regular Noetherian $B$ are domains, so its finitely many irreducible components are disjoint and open; work on the integral component containing $Z$. By the regular prime-divisor lemma, near each point of $Z$, on an open $B_0$, the ideal of $Z$ is generated by one element $t$, prime in every local ring at points of $Z$, and $t$ is a uniformizer of the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{B,s}$. Off $Z$ it is a unit, and points of $Z$ other than $s$ have local dimension at least two. Hence $\operatorname{div}(t)=[Z]$ on $B_0$, so by the dictionary $t$ is a local equation of the Cartier divisor of $[Z]$, and $p^*[Z]$ has local equation $p^*t$. Its zero subspace is $X_{B_0}\times_{B_0}V(t)=p^{-1}(Z)\cap X_{B_0}$, reduced by Step 3. At codimension-one points of $X_{B_0}$ off $|Y|$, $Y=p^{-1}(Z)$, $p^*t$ is a unit. A point $y'\neq\eta_Y$ of $Y$ has codimension at least two: the etale-specialization lemma lifts the strict generization $\eta_Y\leadsto y'$ to a strict generization in a chart, of a point with one-dimensional local ring by Step 5. Now let $A$ be the local ring of an etale chart at a point over $\eta_Y$. It is regular of dimension one by Step 5, and $A/tA$ is the local ring of the induced chart of $Y$, hence reduced; it has dimension zero because $t$ is a nonzero nonunit of the one-dimensional local domain $A$. A reduced zero-dimensional local ring is a field: its unique prime is its maximal ideal, which equals the zero nilradical. So $tA$ is the maximal ideal and the normalized order of $p^*t$ at $\eta_Y$ is one. Therefore $p^*[Z]=[p^{-1}(Z)]$ with multiplicity one; a nonreduced fibre would not give a field quotient.

proof.text: The prime-divisor bijection and Step 6 identify finite integral sums over $B$. A locally finite family of divisors on $X$ has only finitely many members meeting $X_B$: this open is quasi-compact, so a finite subcover of neighborhoods witnessing local finiteness suffices. Distinct global prime divisors meeting an open have distinct nonempty restrictions, since each is the closure of its restriction. By Step 5, a corresponding base prime meets $B$ exactly when its inverse image meets $X_B$. Thus the inverse family is locally finite on $S$. In the forward direction, a neighborhood in $S$ meeting only finitely many base primes pulls back to a neighborhood meeting only those finitely many inverse-image primes. On overlaps of affine opens the local identifications agree, by the uniqueness in Step 5. Consequently the coefficient bijections glue to the stated isomorphism on locally finite sums. The Cartier descriptions also glue: sections of $\mathcal K^\times/\mathcal O^\times$ are sheaf sections, and the dictionary on $B$ and $X_B$ identifies their restrictions with these same Weil sums. Pullback is additive because local equations multiply. This proves the isomorphism and its locality on $S$.

proof.text: Let $a:S'\to S$ be etale. Etale maps are smooth, so on affine etale charts smooth regular ascent makes $S'$ regular locally Noetherian. They are open and hence $V'=a^{-1}V$ is dense by exactly the nonempty-open argument of Step 2. The chartwise calculus preserves smoothness and local finite presentation of $p'$; its separatedness follows by separated base change and its quasi-compactness by quasi-compact base change. Thus it is of finite presentation. Every geometric fibre of $p'$ is a geometric fibre of $p$ after the canonical fibre-product identification, so is nonempty integral. All previous steps therefore apply to $p'$, without any quasi-compactness or separatedness assumption on $a$. For compatibility, work on affine opens and etale charts where a Cartier divisor has local equation $t$. Both routes in the square of divisor groups pull $t$ back by the same composite ring map, by the fibre-product identity; changing $t$ by a regular unit changes both answers by its pulled-back unit. The dictionary's flat-pullback clause identifies these Cartier computations with the Weil groups. Summing and restricting as in Step 7 gives the commutative square globally, even when an etale pullback of a prime divisor splits into several primes.
